title: Shooting Falcon with One Fault: A Practical Rowhammer-Based Fault Attack Against Falcon
evidence_span: The work presents a Rowhammer-based one-single-bit-flip fault attack against Falcon, identifies a vulnerable address offset, optimizes a Hidden Parallelepiped Problem attack, and reports secret-key recovery on Falcon-512 with 250k faulty signatures and an 800x reduction in faulty-signature requirement relative to the state of the art.
problem: Falcon's resistance to practical memory fault attacks is insufficiently understood despite its post-quantum security role.
method_or_artifact: Rowhammer-induced single-bit fault, vulnerable-address discovery, and optimized HPP cryptanalytic recovery workflow.
workload_or_benchmark: Falcon-512 reference implementation and faulty-signature collection; memory layout, platform, hammering parameters, and signature-processing conditions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: DRAM Rowhammer fault injection against a Falcon implementation; device generation, refresh policy, memory placement, and attacker privileges are unspecified.
metrics: 800x fewer required faulty signatures than state of the art
limits: The description does not state attack success probability, hammering time, privilege model, DRAM platforms, or repeatability.
The 800x comparison requires matched implementation and fault-model conditions.
Official description only; cryptanalytic and hardware claims require paper-level review.

title: Slcross: Cross-Component System-Level Cache Side-Channel Attacks on Apple M2 SoC
evidence_span: Slcross reverse-engineers Apple M2 System-Level Cache mechanisms to demonstrate CPU-to-GPU cross-component cache attacks, including a covert channel and an attack on an LLM embedding table during local inference; the official description provides no leakage rate, accuracy, noise, or privilege measurements.
problem: Fine-grained cache side channels across heterogeneous processing units remain insufficiently characterized on Apple silicon.
method_or_artifact: Reverse-engineered SLC mechanisms enabling GPU-to-CPU covert communication and inference-time embedding-table attack.
workload_or_benchmark: Apple M2 SoC with local LLM inference and an embedding-table target; model, cache configuration, attack noise, and observation window are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Apple M2 heterogeneous CPU/GPU SoC and shared system-level cache; OS version, permissions, core allocation, and hardware revision are unspecified.
metrics: Covert channel and sensitive GPU-information leakage demonstrated qualitatively; rates, accuracy, and sample complexity are not provided.
limits: No bandwidth, error rate, attack accuracy, privilege requirement, or mitigation analysis is supplied.
The generality beyond Apple M2 and the selected LLM embedding workload is unknown.
Official description only; security claims require full-paper and independent review.

title: PIMA-SecDB: Processing-in-Memory Acceleration for Fully Homomorphic Encryption Databases
evidence_span: PIMA-SecDB co-designs a multi-level, multi-channel PIM architecture with FHE database algorithms, removes costly circuit bootstrapping from structured queries, and selects PIM-friendly encryption parameters; experiments report 1.98x to 7.93x speedup over existing FHE accelerators.
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption protects outsourced database data but makes encrypted full-scan queries slow.
method_or_artifact: High-bandwidth multi-level/multi-channel PIM architecture, bootstrapping-reduced FHE SQL, and quantitative parameter selection for PIM suitability.
workload_or_benchmark: FHE database operations and structured queries; dataset, query mix, encryption scheme, security level, and accelerator configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Processing-in-memory architecture for encrypted database scans with parallel channels; memory technology, process, frequency, and power boundary are unspecified.
limits: Security parameters, bootstrapping semantics, query workload, dataset scale, and baseline implementations are not supplied.
Speedup range may reflect different query or parameter settings; no energy/area/accuracy-equivalent cost is given.
Official description only; FHE correctness and performance claims require paper-level verification.

title: Are They All Safe? Practical Fault Injection Attacks on FPGA Logic Synthesis Tools
evidence_span: DefVul-Risk builds a defect knowledge base, uses LLMs to generate triggerable HDL vulnerability samples, fine-tunes risk-assessment models, and reports 26 submitted CVE reports with 9 officially confirmed for FPGA synthesis-tool fault-injection risk assessment.
problem: Malicious HDL injection and synthesis-tool flaws can create vulnerabilities in FPGA systems used in critical deployments, while manual toolchain risk assessment does not scale.
method_or_artifact: Automated defect knowledge base, LLM-generated triggerable vulnerability samples, and fine-tuned risk-prioritization model.
workload_or_benchmark: FPGA logic-synthesis tools and vulnerability/CVE assessment; tool versions, vulnerability classes, sample corpus, and evaluation protocol are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FPGA EDA toolchain and HDL input flow; target FPGA families, synthesis settings, and attacker capabilities are unspecified.
baselines: Manual or conventional synthesis-tool security assessment
limits: Submission and confirmation counts do not establish recall, precision, exploitability, or remediation time.
The description omits model evaluation, tool/version coverage, and human-validation procedure.
Official description only; security claims require detailed reproduction and independent review.

title: METRIC: An MDS-Analog ECC with Minimum Two-Column Redundancy for Fault-Tolerant, Layer-Aware IMC Architecture
evidence_span: MECA-CIM uses a two-redundancy-column MDS error-correction framework for analog memristor CIM, allocates protection by Hessian-trace sensitivity, and decodes syndromes in the analog domain; the official description reports robust outlier resistance across CNNs and Transformers with large AEDP reduction over conventional ECC systems.
problem: Memristor analog CIM suffers device defects and circuit noise that create large outliers beyond small-error tolerance.
method_or_artifact: Two-column MDS ECC, Hessian-trace layer sensitivity for adaptive protection allocation, and an analog-domain syndrome decoder.
workload_or_benchmark: CNN and Transformer analog-CIM workloads with defect/noise outlier injection; models, fault distributions, and accuracy criteria are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Memristor crossbar analog CIM with layer-aware redundancy columns and analog syndrome logic; device technology, ADC/peripheral costs, and process conditions are unspecified.
baselines: conventional ECC systems for analog CIM
metrics: Robust outlier resistance across CNNs and Transformers claimed qualitatively
limits: No numeric AEDP, accuracy, fault rate, latency, area, or energy values are provided.
The outlier model, decoder precision, analog noise, and baseline ECC overhead are unspecified.
Official description only; reliability and quality claims require paper-level verification.
